contentHtml:
When the robot vacuum dies and the floor pays the price, I can get it going again. A robot vacuum is really a little computer with motors and sensors bolted on, which is right up my alley. I diagnose and repair charging, docking, sensor and motor faults across all the major brands, for people around Stretton and Brisbane, drop-off or onsite, with an honest quote and no pressure.

The faults I see most

  • Won't charge or dock. Usually dirty charging contacts, a worn dock sensor, or a failing charging circuit.
  • Battery won't hold charge. Like any rechargeable pack, they wear out over time and eventually need replacing.
  • Sensor and mapping trouble. Bumping into things it used to dodge, getting lost, or refusing to map a room.
  • Brush and wheel motor issues. Tangled hair and debris are the usual cause, and sometimes the motor itself has had enough.

Worth fixing before you replace it

A lot of robot vacuums get thrown out over a fault that costs a fraction of a new one to put right. I check it over first and tell you honestly whether it is worth repairing, so you are not sinking money into a lost cause or binning a machine that had years left in it. For other gadgets and hardware, see my hardware repair service.

Send me the details for a quote or call 0477 319 160, with no call-out fee anywhere on Stretton.
